newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toyota no comment on battery sale to Ford.
newsitem.headline: Toyota no comment on battery sale to Ford.

text.p: Toyota Motor Corp and Matsushita Electric Industrial Co Ltd had no comment on Tuesday on a domestic media report that Ford Motor Co would buy electric batteries made by a venture of the two firms for use in Ford's electric vehicles.

The Nihon Keizai Shimbun, an economic daily, reported that Ford would buy nickel-metal hydride rechargeable batteries, made by Panasonic EV Energy Co Ltd, for use in its electric-powered cars to be launched in October 1998 in the United States.
Panasonic EV Energy, owned 60 percent by Matsushita group firms and 40 percent by Toyota, was formed in Kosai, Shizuoka, central Japan, last Wednesday.

Toyota and Matsushita said that the venture's batteries would be marketed to car makers both in Japan and abroad. The battery venture hopes to achieve greater economies of scale by selling to Toyota's rivals as well.
